title: Measuring Endogenous 24(S),25-Epoxycholesterol in Mouse Macrophages
author: Liu, Jin, et al.
materials: This step outlines the procedure for preparing samples for mass spectrometric (MS) measurement. Consequently, the hexane and isopropanol used should be of LC-MS grade, and the 2 mL EP tube should be of low binding quality. Prior to cell harvesting, ensure that the hexane and isopropanol are pre-cooled to −20°C and kept over 8 h.1.Digest the mature BMDMs following the previous steps and count the cells using the TC20 Automated Cell Counter (Bio-Rad) according to the manufacturer’s instruction.2.Adjust 1 × 107 cells to a 100 mm dish and culture the cells in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2. Each group requires at least 5 replicates.3.After resting for 24 h, the BMDMs are either harvested directly or treated for the indicated durations.4.Mix the pre-cooled hexane (0.6 volume) and isopropanol (0.4 volume) thoroughly and place the mixture on ice prior to use.5.Remove the medium from the dish and wash the BMDMs twice with pre-chilled 0.9% saline.Note: Sodium chloride is dissolved in ultra-pure H2O and sterilized using a 0.22 μm syringe filter. Store at 4°C prior to use.6.Add 1 mL of the hexane/isopropanol mixture to the dish and quickly scrape the cells with a cell scraper on ice, then transfer the contents to a new 2 mL EP tube.CRITICAL: Since the organic mixture is prone to volatilization, this process must be conducted swiftly, with a duration of less than 30 s being ideal. To prevent operational errors, the routes and times for scraping each dish should be kept similar.7.Vortex the scraped mixture at the highest speed for 3 min and chill the EP tube on ice for 2 min.8.Centrifuge the samples at 15,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.9.Delicately draw the organic supernatants into a new EP tube and then place it on ice.Note: After centrifugation, the mixture separates, carefully transfer the supernatants to a new tube. To avoid contamination by sediments, it is advised to leave approximately 50 μL of supernatant residue.10.Open the tube and dry the mixture thoroughly by blowing nitrogen gas using Reacti-Vap Evaporators (Thermo Scientific).Note: The dried sample is subjected to following measurement immediately or can be stored at −80°C for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare BMDM culture medium (BMDM‑CM), ACK lysis buffer, and FACS staining buffer according to standard formulations.

steps.title: Euthanize mice and harvest bones
steps.instruction: Euthanize C57BL/6J mice with CO₂, dissect femur and tibia from hind legs after removing skin and tissues.

steps.title: Disinfect and cut bones
steps.instruction: Submerge each bone in 75 % ethanol for 1–2 min, rinse twice with 1 × PBS, then cut each bone into two fragments at the arthrosis site.

steps.title: Flush bone marrow cells
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL syringe with a 25 G needle, flush marrow from each fragment with 1 × PBS into a 100 mm dish; repeat five times per side.

steps.title: Disperse, filter, and centrifuge cells
steps.instruction: Pipette the cell suspension up and down 10 times with a 1 mL pipette, filter through a 70 µm strainer into a 50 mL tube, then centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 25 °C.

steps.title: ACK lysis and wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ACK lysis buffer for 1 min, add 5 mL PBS to quench, and centrifuge again at 300 × g for 5 min at 25 °C.

steps.title: Seed cells for differentiation
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 25 mL BMDM‑CM and plate into two 6‑well plates; incubate at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Feed cultures on day three
steps.instruction: Add an additional 2 mL BMDM‑CM to each well on the third day of culture.

steps.title: Harvest differentiated BMDMs
steps.instruction: On day five, digest cells with 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA (300 µL per well) for 5 min at 37 °C, quench with 1 mL BMDM‑CM, then centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 25 °C.

steps.title: Prepare single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL FACS staining buffer, filter through a 100 µm strainer to obtain a single‑cell suspension.

steps.title: Block Fc receptors
steps.instruction: Incubate cells with mouse anti‑CD16/32 antibody (5 µg/mL) for 10 min at 25 °C, then wash twice with FACS staining buffer (300 × g, 5 min, 25 °C).

steps.title: Stain surface markers
steps.instruction: Stain cells in FACS buffer with Zombie NIR dye, anti‑F4/80‑FITC (5 µg/mL) and anti‑CD11b‑PE (5 µg/mL) for 30 min at 4 °C in the dark, then wash twice as above.

steps.title: Acquire and analyze flow data
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in FACS buffer, analyze on a BD LSR Fortessa X‑20, and process fluorescence data with FlowJo X10.0.7r2.

steps.title: Prepare chilled organic solvents
steps.instruction: Pre‑cool LC‑MS grade hexane and isopropanol to –20 °C for at least 8 h; mix 0.6 volume hexane with 0.4 volume isopropanol and keep on ice.

steps.title: Plate cells for cholesterol assay
steps.instruction: Digest mature BMDMs as previously, count with a TC20, and seed 1 × 10⁷ cells into each 100 mm dish; incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Use ≥5 replicates per group.

steps.title: Wash cells with chilled saline
steps.instruction: After 24 h resting (or after any treatment), remove medium and wash cells twice with pre‑chilled 0.9 % NaCl solution (ultrapure water, 0.22 µm filtered, stored at 4 °C).

steps.title: Extract lipids with solvent
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL hexane/isopropanol mixture to each dish, scrape cells on ice, and transfer the suspension to a low‑binding 2 mL EP tube; complete within 30 s.

steps.title: Vortex and chill extracts
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube at maximum speed for 3 min, then place on ice for 2 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, carefully transfer the organic supernatant to a new EP tube leaving ~50 µL residue, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Dry and store samples
steps.instruction: Evaporate the supernatant to dryness under nitrogen using a Reacti‑Vap evaporator; analyze immediately or store at –80 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Process data and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Analyze flow cytometry data with FlowJo, process MS data with Agilent MassHunter Quantitative Analysis, and conduct statistical analysis in GraphPad Prism 8.0.1 using mean ± SEM, unpaired t‑test, one‑ or two‑way ANOVA with Tukey’s post‑test as appropriate.

description: Innate immune memory refers to the memory status that is ready for responding to the encountering specific or irrelevant secondary stimuli,2 and this state is primarily characterized by epigenetic reprogramming.3 In this protocol, we take advantage of assay for transposase accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) to examine chromatin accessibility and to characterize innate immune memory with enhanced openness.4 Whole glucan particles (WGP) are a well-established inducer of trained immunity1,5 and serve as a positive control here for ATAC-seq assay. We conducted all the assays using mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) and the experiments were approved by Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) of Sun Yat-sen University.
